subject: Oceanography
title: CO₂ Exchange at the Surface
description: A fast breakdown of CO₂ Exchange at the Surface for builders.

hook.text: The ocean absorbs about 25% of human CO₂ emissions every year—a massive invisible carbon sink.

buildup.text: CO₂ dissolves into surface water when atmospheric levels are higher than oceanic levels—diffusion does the work.

discovery.text: Cold water absorbs more CO₂ than warm water—so polar oceans are the biggest sinks.

twist.text: As the ocean warms, it absorbs CO₂ less efficiently—weakening the very sink we depend on.

climax.text: Some models predict the ocean could shift from net sink to net source later this century.

punchline.text: The ocean's appetite for carbon is shrinking—just when we need it most.

quiz.question: How much of human CO₂ emissions does the ocean absorb?
